title: Learn Swing Dance! Lindy Hop for Beginners: Charleston Rhythm (Class 1 of 6)

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: Two instructors break down fundamental swing rhythms with a friendly, conversational approach, guiding students through solo practice before adding music. They emphasize exploring rhythm and weight shifts rather than rigid mechanics.

lesson_structure.note: Instructors introduce themselves and the beginner lesson.
Solo rhythm exploration and walking around the room.
Practicing the basic rhythm with music playing.
Explanation of weight shifts and timing counts.

steps_taught.name: Charleston Rhythm / Basic
steps_taught.description: Stepping and shifting weight to a steady 1-2 count with freedom of movement.

what_works: Built-in practice time with music without needing to touch recording devices
Clear physical demonstration of solo movement first
what_hinders: Lack of mirrored angles makes visual imitation harder

quotes.text: This is a beginner swing dance lesson.
Which foot you are choosing to start with has no meaning right now.
Two counts per step or two counts per weight shift.
We got a lot of the freedom.

evidence_segments.observation: Instructor steps side to side and moves across the room in solo rhythm practice.
Instructors dance solo to music, moving in place and walking around.

extraction.distinctive_method: Encouraging students to walk around the room in solo practice to discover different directions before introducing partner work.
